environment.storage: Local NVMe for all biological inputs, references, outputs and scratch

method: STAR-SLAM on the GRAND-SLAM 100K human fixture, preserving the external SNP BED and STAR arguments. The wrapper post-run comparison now uses the accepted from_nosnp oracle that was already used by the prior campaign acceptance check. Pearson new-to-total correlations are reported at minimum read counts 20, 50 and 100. The small-fixture wall includes index loading and one reference comparison. The corrected 1.9.5 tag was built with the accepted benchmark recipe and one SHA256-identified binary was used everywhere. Scientific arguments, input formats, reference content, hash caches, and caller settings were preserved. Each arm ran once on a quiet host, with fresh outputs and a fatal cold-cache preflight. All input, reference, output, temporary and spill locations were checked against the intended storage. Comparator outputs and times were retained; no comparator was rerun. Completion, executed-command identity, the 1.30 maximum timing ratio, and canonical correlation/cell-call tolerances were checked before scheduling the next arm. Byte equality is a recorded diagnostic rather than an acceptance gate.
limitations: One timed execution per arm, not a replicated distribution.
Retained comparator outputs are comparison evidence rather than ground truth.
Wall times depend on the recorded CPU, storage and cache conditions.
The previous wrapper used a superseded post-run oracle; its accepted canonical parity is the comparison baseline. The new wrapper corrects that validation path without changing STAR arguments.
